title.en: Health Insurance for DACA Recipients 2026 | CoveredUSA
title.es: Seguro Medico para Beneficiarios de DACA 2026 | CoveredUSA

description.en: DACA recipients lost ACA Marketplace access Aug 2026. Employer plans, state Medicaid (CA, NM, WA, OR), FQHCs, and HSA options for Dreamers in 2026.
description.es: Beneficiarios DACA perdieron acceso al Mercado ACA en 2026. Planes del empleador, Medicaid estatal, FQHC y opciones HSA para Dreamers en 2026.

h1.en: Health Insurance for DACA Recipients in 2026
h1.es: Seguro Medico para Beneficiarios de DACA en 2026

subhero.en: The 2025 CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule removed DACA recipients from ACA Marketplace eligibility. In 2026, Dreamers must rely on employer-sponsored plans, state-funded Medicaid programs in California, New Mexico, Washington, and Oregon, or Federally Qualified Health Centers on a sliding-scale basis.
subhero.es: La Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado 2025 del CMS elimino a los beneficiarios de DACA de la elegibilidad del Mercado del ACA. En 2026, los Dreamers deben depender de planes del empleador, programas Medicaid estatales en California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington y Oregon, o Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente con escala de tarifas variables.

quickAnswer.en: DACA recipients, also called Dreamers, cannot buy ACA Marketplace plans or receive Premium Tax Credits in 2026 following the CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule that took effect August 25, 2025. The primary coverage paths are: employer-sponsored health insurance through your Employment Authorization Document (EAD or I-766), which remains fully available; state-funded Medicaid programs in California (Medi-Cal, enrollment frozen for new adult applicants after January 1, 2026), New Mexico (state DACA Coverage Program), Washington (Apple Health for limited categories), and Oregon (OHP Healthier Oregon); and Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) nationwide for sliding-scale primary care regardless of immigration status. DACA recipients who obtain employer-sponsored coverage with an HDHP can still open and contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA) in 2026.
quickAnswer.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA, tambien llamados Dreamers, no pueden comprar planes del Mercado del ACA ni recibir Creditos Fiscales de Prima en 2026, tras la Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado CMS efectiva el 25 de agosto de 2025. Los principales caminos de cobertura son: seguro de salud del empleador a traves de su Documento de Autorizacion de Empleo (EAD o I-766), que sigue disponible; programas Medicaid estatales en California (Medi-Cal), Nuevo Mexico, Washington y Oregon; y Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente (FQHC) a escala de tarifas variables independientemente del estatus migratorio.

introParagraphs.en: DACA recipients, often called Dreamers, held a brief window of ACA Marketplace access from November 1, 2024, through August 25, 2025, under the Biden administration's rule clarifying deferred action as a form of lawful presence. The Trump administration reversed that rule through the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule, published June 25, 2025, which stripped DACA recipients from the definition of lawfully present for purposes of ACA Marketplace enrollment, Premium Tax Credits, cost-sharing reductions, and Basic Health Programs. As of the 2026 plan year, approximately 10,000 Dreamers lost Marketplace coverage and must piece together noncitizen health coverage from other sources. The good news is that DACA recipients still have work authorization via their Employment Authorization Documents, which opens employer-sponsored health insurance as the most stable 2026 option.
introParagraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA, frecuentemente llamados Dreamers, tuvieron una breve ventana de acceso al Mercado del ACA del 1 de noviembre de 2024 al 25 de agosto de 2025 bajo la regla de la administracion Biden. La administracion Trump revirtio esa regla a traves de la Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado 2025, publicada el 25 de junio de 2025, que elimino a los beneficiarios de DACA de la definicion de presencia legal para inscripcion en el Mercado, Creditos Fiscales de Prima, reducciones de costos compartidos y Programas Basicos de Salud. Alrededor de 10,000 Dreamers perdieron cobertura del Mercado y deben buscar cobertura noncitizen de otras fuentes.

introParagraphs.en: Undocumented immigrants and noncitizens with deferred action status face a coverage landscape that is heavily state-dependent. Four states have created meaningful programs using state-only funding that explicitly cover DACA recipients or other immigrants not considered lawfully present under federal rules: California, New Mexico, Washington, and Oregon. Beyond state programs, employer-sponsored insurance remains fully available to any DACA recipient with a valid EAD, and Federally Qualified Health Centers operate on a sliding-fee-scale basis for any patient regardless of immigration status. Form 7206 does not apply to DACA recipients in most cases, because most Dreamers are W-2 employees rather than self-employed sole proprietors. For DACA recipients who do operate as independent contractors or sole proprietors, the self-employment health insurance deduction via Form 7206 is available only on qualifying coverage, and Marketplace plans are no longer qualifying coverage in 2026.
introParagraphs.es: Los inmigrantes sin documentos y los noncitizens con estatus de accion diferida enfrentan un panorama de cobertura altamente dependiente del estado. Cuatro estados han creado programas significativos usando fondos exclusivamente estatales que cubren explicitamente a los beneficiarios de DACA: California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington y Oregon. Mas alla de los programas estatales, el seguro de salud del empleador sigue disponible para cualquier beneficiario de DACA con un EAD valido, y los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente operan con escala de tarifas variables para cualquier paciente independientemente del estatus migratorio.

footnote.en: ACA Marketplace plans and Premium Tax Credits are not available to DACA recipients in 2026 following the CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule (effective August 25, 2025). DACA recipients in Washington state may have limited access through state-funded Cascade Care Savings at up to 250% FPL.
footnote.es: Los planes del Mercado del ACA y los Creditos Fiscales de Prima no estan disponibles para los beneficiarios de DACA en 2026 tras la Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado del CMS (efectiva el 25 de agosto de 2025). Los beneficiarios de DACA en Washington pueden tener acceso limitado a traves del Cascade Care Savings financiado por el estado hasta el 250% FPL.

optionsOverview.source: CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule (June 25, 2025), HealthCare.gov, KFF, New Mexico Health Care Authority

heading.en: Option 1: Employer-Sponsored Health Insurance Through Your EAD
heading.es: Opcion 1: Seguro de Salud del Empleador a Traves de su EAD

paragraphs.en: Employer-sponsored health insurance is the most stable and often the most affordable coverage path for DACA recipients in 2026. A valid Employment Authorization Document (EAD, Form I-766) grants the same right to work and to participate in group health benefit plans as any other worker. Employers are legally barred from discriminating in benefits based on immigration status when a worker is otherwise authorized to work, meaning a Dreamer on a valid EAD has equal access to the same group health plan as their coworkers.
paragraphs.es: El seguro de salud del empleador es el camino de cobertura mas estable y frecuentemente mas asequible para los beneficiarios de DACA en 2026. Un Documento de Autorizacion de Empleo valido (EAD, Formulario I-766) otorga el mismo derecho a trabajar y participar en planes de beneficios de salud grupales que cualquier otro trabajador. Los empleadores estan legalmente prohibidos de discriminar en beneficios por estatus migratorio cuando un trabajador esta autorizado a trabajar.

paragraphs.en: Group employer plans cover all 10 ACA essential health benefits and cannot exclude pre-existing conditions. Premium costs are shared between employer and employee, and employee contributions are deducted pretax through payroll under Section 125, reducing taxable income. For a Dreamer working full-time at a company offering family coverage, joining the employer plan typically costs $150 to $600 per month out of pocket for employee-plus-family enrollment, compared to full-sticker private insurance of $500 to $1,800 per month. The enrollment window is the employer's annual open enrollment period plus qualifying life events triggering a special election period of typically 30 to 60 days.
paragraphs.es: Los planes de grupo del empleador cubren los 10 beneficios esenciales de salud del ACA y no pueden excluir condiciones preexistentes. Los costos de prima se comparten entre el empleador y el empleado, y las contribuciones del empleado se deducen antes de impuestos a traves de la nomina, reduciendo el ingreso gravable. Para un Dreamer que trabaja a tiempo completo en una empresa con cobertura familiar, inscribirse en el plan del empleador tipicamente cuesta $150 a $600 al mes de su bolsillo para inscripcion del empleado mas familia.

heading.en: Option 2: State-Funded Medicaid Programs for DACA Recipients
heading.es: Opcion 2: Programas Medicaid Estatales para Beneficiarios de DACA

paragraphs.en: Four states have built coverage programs using state-only funds that explicitly extend to DACA recipients and undocumented immigrants who cannot access federally-funded Medicaid. California's Medi-Cal program historically covered income-eligible immigrants of all statuses but froze new enrollments for undocumented adults age 19 and older after January 1, 2026. DACA recipients who were already enrolled in Medi-Cal before that date retain coverage; new adult applicants as of 2026 are no longer accepted. Emergency Medi-Cal (Emergency Medicaid under California's state program) remains available for acute stabilization regardless of enrollment date or immigration status. Children under 19 and pregnant individuals remain eligible to apply for full Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status.
paragraphs.es: Cuatro estados han creado programas usando fondos exclusivamente estatales que se extienden a los beneficiarios de DACA. Medi-Cal de California historicamente cubrio a inmigrantes elegibles por ingresos de todos los estatus, pero congelo nuevas inscripciones para adultos indocumentados de 19 anos o mas despues del 1 de enero de 2026. Los beneficiarios de DACA que ya estaban inscritos en Medi-Cal antes de esa fecha mantienen su cobertura.

paragraphs.en: New Mexico launched a dedicated 2026 DACA Coverage Program through the New Mexico Health Care Authority, offering state-funded premium assistance on a sliding scale based on household income for DACA recipients who lost Marketplace access. Eligible Dreamers in New Mexico can enroll through the dedicated state portal at easigov.com/daca.html. Washington state has a state-funded Cascade Care Savings program that extends to income-eligible DACA recipients earning up to 250% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level ($39,900 for a single person). Oregon's OHP Healthier Oregon program uses state funds to cover income-eligible residents regardless of immigration status at or below 138% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level ($22,025 for a single person), and DACA recipients in Oregon qualify on income grounds alone. These state programs have separate income limits and application processes from federal Medicaid.
paragraphs.es: Nuevo Mexico lanzo un Programa de Cobertura DACA 2026 dedicado, ofreciendo asistencia de primas financiada por el estado en escala variable segun el ingreso del hogar para los beneficiarios de DACA que perdieron acceso al Mercado. Washington tiene un programa Cascade Care Savings que se extiende a beneficiarios de DACA con ingresos hasta el 250% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026. El programa OHP Healthier Oregon usa fondos estatales para cubrir a residentes elegibles por ingresos independientemente del estatus migratorio hasta el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026.

heading.es: Opcion 3: Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente (FQHC)

paragraphs.en: Federally Qualified Health Centers are federally funded community health centers required by law to serve every patient regardless of immigration status or ability to pay. FQHCs set fees on a sliding scale based on household income relative to the Federal Poverty Level, with patients at or below 100% FPL paying nominal fees of approximately $20 to $50 per visit, and no patient turned away for inability to pay. FQHCs are not insurance and do not cover hospital admissions or specialist referrals outside the FQHC's own services, but they provide primary care, preventive care, dental, behavioral health, and some specialty services in-house.
paragraphs.es: Los Centros de Salud Calificados Federalmente son centros de salud comunitarios financiados federalmente y obligados por ley a atender a cada paciente independientemente del estatus migratorio o la capacidad de pago. Los FQHC establecen tarifas en escala variable segun el ingreso del hogar relativo al Nivel Federal de Pobreza, con pacientes al 100% FPL o menos pagando tarifas nominales de aproximadamente $20 a $50 por visita.

paragraphs.en: For DACA recipients without employer coverage and without access to a qualifying state Medicaid program, FQHCs represent the most accessible safety net for routine care. Find the nearest FQHC through findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov. Emergency care is separately protected under EMTALA: any hospital receiving Medicare or Medicaid funds must provide emergency screening and stabilization regardless of immigration status or ability to pay. Neither FQHC visits nor EMTALA stabilization count against a public charge determination under current 2026 DHS regulations.
paragraphs.es: Para los beneficiarios de DACA sin cobertura del empleador y sin acceso a un programa Medicaid estatal calificado, los FQHC representan la red de seguridad mas accesible para atencion rutinaria. La atencion de emergencia esta protegida por separado bajo EMTALA: cualquier hospital que recibe fondos de Medicare o Medicaid debe proporcionar evaluacion de emergencia y estabilizacion independientemente del estatus migratorio.

heading.es: Opcion 4: Seguro Privado de Compra Directa

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients can purchase health insurance directly from private insurers outside the ACA Marketplace in all 50 states. Off-Marketplace private insurance plans are not required to accept all applicants in every situation, but most individual market carriers in the United States follow ACA guaranteed-issue and no-pre-existing-condition-exclusion rules voluntarily or by state law even for off-Marketplace sales. The significant downside is cost: without Marketplace subsidies or Premium Tax Credits, full-premium individual plans run $400 to $1,100 per month for a single adult in 2026 depending on age, plan tier, and state. If the private plan qualifies as an HSA-eligible HDHP (minimum deductible $1,700 individual or $3,400 family in 2026 per Rev. Proc. 2025-19), the DACA recipient can open and fund a Health Savings Account.
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA pueden comprar seguro de salud directamente de aseguradoras privadas fuera del Mercado del ACA en los 50 estados. Los planes privados fuera del Mercado no requieren subsidios ni Creditos Fiscales de Prima, pero a costo completo los planes individuales cuestan $400 a $1,100 al mes para un adulto soltero en 2026. Si el plan privado califica como un HDHP compatible con HSA (deducible minimo de $1,700 individual o $3,400 familia en 2026 per Rev. Proc. 2025-19), el beneficiario de DACA puede abrir y financiar una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud.

intro.en: DACA recipients are frequently targeted by insurance products that look like health coverage but leave them unprotected. Avoid these in 2026:
intro.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA frecuentemente son blanco de productos que parecen cobertura de salud pero los dejan desprotegidos. Evite estos en 2026:

en: Assuming Marketplace plans are still an option

The 2025 CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule removed DACA recipients from lawfully-present status for Marketplace purposes. Attempting to enroll by misrepresenting immigration status constitutes fraud and can jeopardize DACA renewal. There is no legitimate path to Premium Tax Credits for Dreamers in 2026.
es: Suponer que los planes del Mercado siguen siendo una opcion

La Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado CMS 2025 elimino a los beneficiarios de DACA del estatus de presencia legal para el Mercado. Intentar inscribirse falsificando el estatus migratorio constituye fraude y puede poner en riesgo la renovacion del DACA.

en: NOT insurance. No legal obligation to pay. Pre-existing conditions excluded. Lifestyle clauses can disqualify care. DACA recipients paying into these programs have no recourse if a claim is denied.
es: Ministerios de compartir salud (Medi-Share, Liberty HealthShare)

NO son seguro. Ninguna obligacion legal de pagar. Condiciones preexistentes excluidas. Clausulas de estilo de vida pueden descalificar la atencion. Los beneficiarios de DACA que pagan estos programas no tienen recurso si se niega un reclamo.

en: Short-term limited-duration plans sold as ACA alternatives

Do not cover pre-existing conditions, can be rescinded retroactively, and do not qualify as minimum essential coverage. A hospitalization on one of these plans can result in a six-figure bill with no protection.
es: Planes de corto plazo de duracion limitada vendidos como alternativas al ACA

No cubren condiciones preexistentes, pueden cancelarse retroactivamente y no califican como cobertura esencial minima. Una hospitalizacion con uno de estos planes puede resultar en una factura de seis cifras sin proteccion.

en: Discount cards are NOT insurance. They offer negotiated discounts at participating providers but cover nothing. A DACA recipient paying $50 to $150 per month for a 'health discount card' has no actual coverage for serious illness.
es: Las tarjetas de descuento NO son seguro. Ofrecen descuentos negociados en proveedores participantes pero no cubren nada. Un beneficiario de DACA que paga $50 a $150 al mes por una 'tarjeta de descuento de salud' no tiene cobertura real para enfermedades graves.

footnote.en: Verify any plan with the state insurance commissioner's office before purchasing. For DACA recipients, legitimate coverage paths in 2026 are employer-sponsored group plans, state-funded Medicaid programs, direct-purchase ACA-equivalent private plans, and FQHCs for primary care.
footnote.es: Verifique cualquier plan con la oficina del comisionado de seguros del estado antes de comprar. Para los beneficiarios de DACA, los caminos legítimos de cobertura en 2026 son planes de grupo del empleador, programas Medicaid estatales, planes privados de compra directa equivalentes al ACA, y FQHC para atencion primaria.

traps.source: CMS, National Immigration Law Center (NILC), KFF

heading.en: CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule: What Changed for DACA Recipients in 2026
heading.es: Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado CMS: Que Cambio para los Beneficiarios de DACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) published the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule on June 25, 2025. The rule took effect August 25, 2025. One of its central provisions amended the definition of lawfully present for ACA Marketplace purposes to exclude DACA recipients, reinstating the interpretation used in the original 2012 Interim Final Rule. This reversal of the Biden administration's May 2024 rule eliminated DACA recipients' eligibility for Qualified Health Plans (QHPs) through the Marketplace, for Advance Premium Tax Credits (APTC), for cost-sharing reductions (CSRs), and for state Basic Health Programs (BHPs) including Oregon's OHP-as-BHP and New York's Essential Plan. CMS estimates approximately 10,000 Dreamers lost Marketplace coverage and approximately 1,000 lost BHP coverage under this provision.
paragraphs.es: El CMS publico la Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado 2025 el 25 de junio de 2025, con vigencia el 25 de agosto de 2025. La regla modifica la definicion de presencia legal para excluir a los beneficiarios de DACA, eliminando su elegibilidad para Planes Calificados de Salud, Creditos Anticipados de Prima, reducciones de costos compartidos y Programas Basicos de Salud estatales. El CMS estima que aproximadamente 10,000 Dreamers perdieron la cobertura del Mercado.

paragraphs.en: The DACA eligibility provision of this final rule was specifically NOT challenged in the August 2025 court case (City of Columbus plaintiffs) that stayed other provisions of the same rule. As a result, the DACA ineligibility provision is fully in effect for plan year 2026. DACA recipients who were auto-terminated from Marketplace plans received notices and had a Special Enrollment Period to find alternative coverage. Any Dreamer who currently holds a Marketplace plan in 2026 should confirm coverage status directly with their marketplace account; any ongoing enrollment is likely an error and could create future repayment liability.
paragraphs.es: La disposicion de elegibilidad DACA de esta regla NO fue impugnada en el caso judicial de agosto de 2025. Como resultado, la disposicion de inelegibilidad de DACA esta completamente vigente para el ano de plan 2026. Los beneficiarios de DACA que fueron terminados automaticamente de los planes del Mercado recibieron avisos y tuvieron un Periodo de Inscripcion Especial para encontrar cobertura alternativa.

heading.en: State-by-State Coverage Programs for DACA Recipients in 2026
heading.es: Programas de Cobertura Estatales para Beneficiarios de DACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: Coverage options for DACA recipients vary significantly by state because the federal ACA floor no longer applies to Dreamers. States using only state funds can extend Medicaid-equivalent coverage to people not considered lawfully present under federal rules. California's Medi-Cal program covered income-eligible immigrants regardless of immigration status before 2026, but froze new adult (age 19 and older) enrollment after January 1, 2026. DACA recipients already enrolled in Medi-Cal before the freeze continue to receive coverage. California children under age 19 and pregnant individuals remain eligible to apply for full Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status in 2026. The California state income limit for Medi-Cal full-scope coverage is 138% of the Federal Poverty Level: $22,025 for a single person in 2026, $45,540 for a family of four in 2026.
paragraphs.es: Las opciones de cobertura para los beneficiarios de DACA varian significativamente por estado porque el piso del ACA federal ya no aplica a los Dreamers. California congeló nuevas inscripciones de adultos (mayores de 19 anos) en Medi-Cal despues del 1 de enero de 2026. Los beneficiarios de DACA ya inscritos en Medi-Cal antes del congelamiento continuan recibiendo cobertura. El limite de ingresos para cobertura completa de Medi-Cal es el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza: $22,025 para un individuo en 2026.

paragraphs.en: New Mexico's Health Care Authority operates a dedicated 2026 DACA Coverage Program offering state-funded premium assistance on a sliding-scale basis. DACA recipients in New Mexico can enroll through the dedicated state portal at easigov.com/daca.html (call 505-705-3310 for assistance); coverage is a state-funded Clear Cost Gold plan with income-based premium contributions. Washington state's Apple Health (Medicaid) uses state funds to cover certain categories of immigrants; DACA recipients with income at or below 250% FPL ($39,900 single in 2026) may access Cascade Care Savings through the Washington Health Benefit Exchange. Oregon's OHP Healthier Oregon program uses state funds to extend coverage to all income-eligible residents at or below 138% FPL regardless of immigration status, covering DACA recipients on the same income basis as any other Oregon resident ($22,025 for a single person in 2026). Contact cover.oregon.gov for Oregon enrollment.
paragraphs.es: La Autoridad de Salud de Nuevo Mexico opera un Programa de Cobertura DACA 2026 dedicado con asistencia de primas financiada por el estado en escala variable. Los beneficiarios de DACA en Nuevo Mexico pueden inscribirse a traves del portal estatal dedicado en easigov.com/daca.html. Washington cubre a ciertas categorias de inmigrantes con fondos estatales hasta el 250% FPL ($39,900 individual en 2026). Oregon usa fondos estatales para extender cobertura a todos los residentes elegibles por ingresos hasta el 138% FPL sin importar el estatus migratorio ($22,025 para un individuo en 2026).

heading.en: Premium Tax Credit (PTC) Eligibility for DACA Recipients in 2026
heading.es: Elegibilidad para el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) para Beneficiarios de DACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients are not eligible for the Premium Tax Credit (PTC) in 2026. The CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule eliminated Dreamers from the definition of lawfully present for Marketplace purposes, and PTC eligibility is conditioned on being enrolled in a Marketplace Qualified Health Plan. With Marketplace enrollment unavailable to DACA recipients, the PTC pathway is closed. This represents a significant change from the brief November 2024 through August 2025 window when DACA recipients could access APTC. For DACA recipients who enrolled and received APTC during that window, Form 1095-A reconciliation at tax time (via Form 8962) would apply for the months of coverage received.
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA no son elegibles para el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) en 2026. La Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado CMS elimino a los Dreamers del Marketplace. Para los beneficiarios de DACA que se inscribieron y recibieron APTC durante la ventana de noviembre de 2024 a agosto de 2025, aplica la reconciliacion del Formulario 1095-A en la declaracion de impuestos (via Formulario 8962).

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients who obtain employer-sponsored coverage do not receive PTCs in any case, since employer-sponsored coverage makes a worker ineligible for Marketplace PTC even among workers with lawful status. For DACA recipients in states with state-funded coverage programs, any state-specific premium assistance (as in New Mexico's DACA Coverage Program) is not a federal PTC and does not flow through Form 1095-A; it is a state grant equivalent. The income thresholds for state programs vary; New Mexico uses a sliding scale, while California's Medi-Cal uses 138% of the 2026 FPL ($22,025 for a single person, $45,540 for a family of four).
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA que obtienen cobertura del empleador no reciben PTC en ningun caso, ya que la cobertura del empleador hace a un trabajador inelegible para el PTC del Mercado. Para los beneficiarios de DACA en estados con programas de cobertura estatales, cualquier asistencia de prima estatal no es un PTC federal y no fluye a traves del Formulario 1095-A.

heading.en: HSA and HDHP Fit for DACA Recipients in 2026
heading.es: Compatibilidad de HSA y HDHP para Beneficiarios de DACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients who are enrolled in an HSA-eligible High-Deductible Health Plan (HDHP) can open and contribute to a Health Savings Account (HSA) in 2026. Immigration status does not affect HSA eligibility: the IRS requires only that the account holder is enrolled in a qualifying HDHP, has no other disqualifying coverage, and is not enrolled in Medicare. An HDHP in 2026 requires a minimum deductible of $1,700 for self-only coverage or $3,400 for family coverage (per IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-19), with maximum out-of-pocket limits of $8,500 self or $17,000 family. HDHPs are available through both employer-sponsored plans and direct-purchase private insurance.
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA inscritos en un Plan con Deducible Alto (HDHP) elegible para HSA pueden abrir y contribuir a una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud (HSA) en 2026. El estatus migratorio no afecta la elegibilidad para el HSA. Un HDHP en 2026 requiere un deducible minimo de $1,700 para cobertura individual o $3,400 para cobertura familiar (segun IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-19), con limites maximos de gasto de $8,500 individual o $17,000 familiar.

paragraphs.en: The HSA contribution limit for 2026 is $4,400 for self-only coverage or $8,750 for family coverage, plus a $1,000 catch-up contribution for account holders age 55 and older. HSA contributions deliver a triple tax advantage: contributions are tax-deductible (or pre-tax through payroll), growth is tax-free, and qualified medical withdrawals are tax-free. For DACA recipients enrolled in an employer HDHP, contributions through payroll deduction also avoid Social Security and Medicare (FICA) taxes, an additional benefit. Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) are employer-sponsored and not available to people without a W-2 employer offering them; most DACA recipients accessing employer plans will have FSA access if the employer offers it, but FSA is distinct from an HSA: FSA funds are use-it-or-lose-it annually and are not portable, while HSA funds roll over indefinitely.
paragraphs.es: El limite de contribucion HSA para 2026 es $4,400 para cobertura individual o $8,750 para cobertura familiar, mas $1,000 de contribucion adicional para titulares de 55 anos o mas. Las contribuciones HSA ofrecen una triple ventaja fiscal: las contribuciones son deducibles de impuestos, el crecimiento es libre de impuestos y los retiros medicos calificados son libres de impuestos. Las Cuentas de Gastos Flexibles (FSA) son del empleador; los fondos FSA se pierden anualmente si no se usan y no son portables, mientras que los fondos HSA se acumulan indefinidamente.

heading.en: Form 7206 and Self-Employment Tax for DACA Recipients
heading.es: Formulario 7206 e Impuesto al Trabajo por Cuenta Propia para Beneficiarios de DACA

paragraphs.en: Form 7206 does not apply to most DACA recipients because most Dreamers work as W-2 employees rather than self-employed sole proprietors or 1099 contractors. W-2 employees deduct health premiums via pretax payroll if the employer offers a Section 125 cafeteria plan; the Form 7206 above-the-line deduction is reserved for self-employed individuals with net self-employment income and no access to an employer-sponsored plan during the month of coverage.
paragraphs.es: El Formulario 7206 no aplica a la mayoria de los beneficiarios de DACA porque la mayoria de los Dreamers trabajan como empleados W-2 en lugar de propietarios unicos o contratistas 1099. Los empleados W-2 deducen las primas de salud a traves de la nomina antes de impuestos si el empleador ofrece un plan de cafeteria Seccion 125.

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients who do operate as independent contractors or 1099 contractors with net self-employment income should be aware that the self-employed health insurance deduction under Form 7206 is contingent on having qualifying coverage. In 2026, ACA Marketplace plans are not available to DACA recipients, which removes the most common qualifying coverage type. A DACA recipient who is a sole proprietor and purchases qualifying private off-Marketplace insurance or enrolls in a state-funded program that constitutes health insurance can still claim the Form 7206 deduction for premiums paid, provided they have net SE income and were not eligible for any employer plan during the month. Critically, the Form 7206 deduction reduces income tax only; it does NOT reduce self-employment tax on Schedule SE. The 15.3% SE tax (12.4% Social Security plus 2.9% Medicare) is calculated on net SE earnings before the health insurance deduction, and that calculation is unaffected by the Form 7206 deduction.
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA que trabajan como contratistas independientes o 1099 con ingreso neto del trabajo por cuenta propia deben saber que la deduccion del seguro medico para autónomos bajo el Formulario 7206 es contingente a tener cobertura calificada. En 2026, los planes del Mercado del ACA no estan disponibles para los beneficiarios de DACA. Crucialmente, la deduccion del Formulario 7206 reduce el impuesto sobre la renta solamente; NO reduce el impuesto al trabajo por cuenta propia en el Schedule SE. El 15.3% de impuesto SE se calcula sobre las ganancias netas SE antes de la deduccion del seguro medico.

heading.en: Marketplace Special Enrollment Period (SEP) Triggers for DACA Recipients
heading.es: Activadores del Periodo de Inscripcion Especial (SEP) del Mercado para Beneficiarios de DACA

paragraphs.en: ACA Marketplace SEPs are not available to DACA recipients in 2026 for Marketplace plans, because DACA recipients are ineligible for the Marketplace itself. However, SEP-equivalent enrollment windows apply to the coverage options that are available. For employer-sponsored health insurance, most employers offer a qualifying life event (QLE) window of 30 to 60 days from the date of the triggering event, which is similar in design to the Marketplace SEP. For state-funded Medicaid programs (California, New Mexico, Washington, Oregon), enrollment is generally year-round with no open-enrollment restriction.
paragraphs.es: Los SEP del Mercado del ACA no estan disponibles para los beneficiarios de DACA en 2026 para planes del Mercado. Sin embargo, ventanas de inscripcion equivalentes aplican a las opciones de cobertura disponibles. Para el seguro del empleador, la mayoria de los empleadores ofrecen una ventana de evento calificador (QLE) de 30 a 60 dias desde la fecha del evento desencadenante. Para los programas Medicaid estatales, la inscripcion es generalmente durante todo el ano.

paragraphs.en: DACA recipients who lose employer coverage trigger a qualifying event for state Medicaid enrollment in states with open rolling enrollment. The following events open enrollment windows for the available coverage options for Dreamers in 2026: loss of employer health coverage (triggers 30 to 60 day QLE window with a new employer or state Medicaid application), gaining or renewing employment with a benefits-offering employer (triggers employer plan enrollment window), moving to a new state with a DACA-friendly Medicaid program (triggers immediate Medicaid eligibility in CA/NM/WA/OR on a rolling basis), marriage or addition of a dependent (triggers employer QLE window for dependent enrollment), DACA renewal (not itself a triggering event, but renewing work authorization enables continued employer coverage), and income change that places a Dreamer below a state program's income threshold (triggers state Medicaid eligibility).
paragraphs.es: Los beneficiarios de DACA que pierden la cobertura del empleador desencadenan un evento calificador para la inscripcion en Medicaid estatal en estados con inscripcion continua. Los siguientes eventos abren ventanas de inscripcion para los Dreamers en 2026: perdida de la cobertura del empleador, obtener un nuevo empleo con beneficios, mudanza a un nuevo estado con Medicaid favorable para DACA, matrimonio o adicion de un dependiente, renovacion del DACA, y cambio de ingreso por debajo del umbral del programa estatal.

list.en: Loss of employer coverage: 30 to 60 day QLE window for new employer plan or state Medicaid application (CA/NM/WA/OR)
list.es: Perdida de la cobertura del empleador: ventana QLE de 30 a 60 dias para nuevo plan del empleador o solicitud de Medicaid estatal

list.en: Gaining new employment with health benefits: employer open enrollment window (typically 30 days from hire date)
list.es: Obtener nuevo empleo con beneficios de salud: ventana de inscripcion del empleador (tipicamente 30 dias desde la fecha de contratacion)

list.en: Moving to California, New Mexico, Washington, or Oregon: rolling Medicaid eligibility in state-funded programs (year-round applications)
list.es: Mudarse a California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington u Oregon: elegibilidad Medicaid continua en programas estatales (solicitudes durante todo el ano)

list.en: Marriage or domestic partnership: employer QLE window for adding dependent to employer plan
list.es: Matrimonio o union domestica: ventana QLE del empleador para agregar dependiente al plan del empleador

list.en: Birth or adoption of a child: employer QLE for dependent coverage; state Medi-Cal/OHP eligibility for the child regardless of DACA parent's status
list.es: Nacimiento o adopcion de un hijo: QLE del empleador para cobertura de dependiente; elegibilidad de Medi-Cal/OHP estatal para el nino independientemente del estatus DACA del padre

list.en: Income reduction below state Medicaid threshold: rolling state program enrollment in CA/NM/WA/OR based on income recalculation
list.es: Reduccion de ingresos por debajo del umbral de Medicaid estatal: inscripcion continua en el programa estatal en CA/NM/WA/OR basada en recalculo de ingresos

heading.en: How to Apply for Health Coverage as a DACA Recipient in 2026
heading.es: Como Solicitar Cobertura de Salud como Beneficiario de DACA en 2026

paragraphs.en: Applying for health coverage as a Dreamer in 2026 depends on which pathway applies. For employer-sponsored plans, the starting point is the employer's HR department or benefits portal, not HealthCare.gov. Enrollment windows are set by the employer (typically a 30-day new-hire window and an annual open enrollment period). For state Medicaid programs in California, New Mexico, Washington, and Oregon, applications go through the state agency directly. For FQHCs, no prior application is required: walk in or call for an appointment, and the FQHC will assess your income for sliding-scale fees at the first visit.
paragraphs.es: Solicitar cobertura de salud como Dreamer en 2026 depende del camino que aplique. Para planes del empleador, el punto de partida es el departamento de RRHH del empleador, no HealthCare.gov. Para programas Medicaid estatales en California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington y Oregon, las solicitudes se hacen directamente con la agencia estatal. Para los FQHC, no se requiere solicitud previa.

list.en: Step 1: Determine your state and employment situation (W-2 employer with benefits / self-employed 1099 / neither). This determines which coverage path to pursue first.
list.es: Paso 1: Determine su estado y situacion laboral (empleador W-2 con beneficios / autónomo 1099 / ninguno). Esto determina que camino de cobertura seguir primero.

list.en: Step 2: If you have a W-2 employer offering health benefits, contact HR immediately. Ask for a benefits enrollment packet and confirm the enrollment window (usually 30 days from hire date, or annual open enrollment in November/December).
list.es: Paso 2: Si tiene un empleador W-2 con beneficios de salud, contacte a RRHH de inmediato. Solicite el paquete de inscripcion de beneficios y confirme la ventana de inscripcion.

list.en: Step 3: If you are in California, New Mexico, Washington, or Oregon and meet the income thresholds, apply through the state program: Medi-Cal (CoveredCA.com for existing-enrollee renewals or county office for Medi-Cal-only), New Mexico DACA Coverage (easigov.com/daca.html), Apple Health via Washington Healthplanfinder (wahbexchange.org), or OHP via cover.oregon.gov.
list.es: Paso 3: Si esta en California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington u Oregon y cumple con los umbrales de ingresos, solicite a traves del programa estatal: Medi-Cal, Cobertura DACA de Nuevo Mexico (easigov.com/daca.html), Apple Health via Washington Healthplanfinder, o OHP via cover.oregon.gov.

list.en: Step 4: If you are in any other state without employer coverage, locate the nearest FQHC through findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov. FQHC sliding-scale care requires no advance enrollment.
list.es: Paso 4: Si esta en cualquier otro estado sin cobertura del empleador, localice el FQHC mas cercano a traves de findahealthcenter.hrsa.gov. La atencion de escala variable del FQHC no requiere inscripcion previa.

list.en: Step 5: For comprehensive coverage in non-program states, research direct-purchase private insurance. Request quotes from at least 3 carriers. Confirm the plan covers all 10 ACA essential health benefits. If the plan is an HDHP, open an HSA through a bank or credit union.
list.es: Paso 5: Para cobertura integral en estados sin programa, investigue el seguro privado de compra directa. Solicite cotizaciones de al menos 3 aseguradoras. Confirme que el plan cubre los 10 beneficios esenciales del ACA. Si el plan es un HDHP, abra un HSA a traves de un banco o cooperativa de credito.

en.question: Can DACA recipients buy health insurance through the ACA Marketplace in 2026?
en.answer: No. The 2025 CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule, effective August 25, 2025, removed DACA recipients from the definition of lawfully present for ACA Marketplace purposes. Dreamers cannot enroll in Marketplace Qualified Health Plans, receive Premium Tax Credits (PTC or APTC), cost-sharing reductions (CSRs), or access Basic Health Programs through the Marketplace in 2026. This reverses the brief November 2024 through August 2025 window when DACA recipients had Marketplace access under the Biden administration's rule.

en.question: What is the best health insurance option for DACA recipients in 2026?
en.answer: For most Dreamers, employer-sponsored health insurance through a valid Employment Authorization Document (EAD) is the best option in 2026: it covers all 10 essential health benefits, costs are shared with the employer, and premiums are paid pretax. For income-eligible DACA recipients in California, New Mexico, Washington, or Oregon, state-funded Medicaid programs offer comprehensive coverage at low or no cost. DACA recipients in other states without employer coverage should use Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) for primary care on a sliding-scale basis and research direct-purchase private insurance for comprehensive coverage.

en.question: Do DACA recipients qualify for the Premium Tax Credit?
en.answer: No. DACA recipients are not eligible for the federal Premium Tax Credit (PTC) in 2026. PTC eligibility requires enrollment in an ACA Marketplace plan, and DACA recipients cannot enroll in Marketplace plans following the CMS Marketplace Integrity and Affordability Final Rule. For DACA recipients who received APTC during the November 2024 through August 2025 window of Marketplace eligibility, a Form 1095-A and Form 8962 reconciliation will be needed on their 2025 federal tax return to settle any advance payments received.

en.question: Can DACA recipients use a Health Savings Account (HSA)?
en.answer: Yes, if they are enrolled in an HSA-eligible HDHP. Immigration status does not affect HSA eligibility. An HDHP in 2026 has a minimum deductible of $1,700 self or $3,400 family (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-19), and the HSA contribution limit is $4,400 self or $8,750 family, plus a $1,000 catch-up if age 55 or older. HSA contributions are tax-deductible, grow tax-free, and can be withdrawn tax-free for qualified medical expenses. DACA recipients enrolled in an employer HDHP can contribute pretax through payroll. Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA) are employer-only and available to DACA recipients with W-2 employment if the employer offers them.

en.question: Does California still cover DACA recipients in Medi-Cal?
en.answer: California's Medi-Cal continues to cover DACA recipients who were already enrolled before January 1, 2026. After January 1, 2026, California froze new Medi-Cal enrollment for undocumented adults age 19 and older, which includes most DACA recipients applying for the first time. Children under age 19 and pregnant individuals remain eligible to apply for full-scope Medi-Cal regardless of immigration status. The Medi-Cal income limit is 138% of the 2026 Federal Poverty Level: $22,025 for a single person, $45,540 for a family of four.

en.question: When can DACA recipients enroll in coverage outside of open enrollment?
en.answer: For employer-sponsored plans, DACA recipients can enroll or add coverage within 30 to 60 days of a qualifying life event: getting a new job, losing coverage, getting married, having a child, or moving to a new state. For state Medicaid programs in New Mexico, Washington, and Oregon, enrollment is year-round without an open-enrollment restriction. California's Medi-Cal also accepts applications year-round for eligible individuals. Direct-purchase private insurance from carriers can generally be purchased at any time. FQHCs require no prior enrollment.

en.question: Can DACA recipients claim a self-employment health insurance tax deduction?
en.answer: DACA recipients who are sole proprietors or 1099 contractors with net self-employment income may claim the Form 7206 deduction for qualifying health insurance premiums paid, provided they were not eligible for employer-sponsored coverage during the month. In 2026, qualifying coverage would be employer-sponsored plans, private off-Marketplace insurance, or state-funded insurance that constitutes comprehensive health coverage. ACA Marketplace plans are not an option for DACA recipients. Critically, the Form 7206 deduction reduces income tax only and does NOT reduce self-employment tax on Schedule SE. The 15.3% SE tax is calculated separately and is unaffected by the health insurance deduction. Most DACA recipients are W-2 workers; Form 7206 is not relevant for W-2 employees.

en.question: What coverage does Emergency Medicaid provide for DACA recipients?
en.answer: Emergency Medicaid provides federal reimbursement to hospitals for emergency stabilization services provided to individuals who would otherwise qualify for Medicaid but for their immigration status. DACA recipients can receive emergency stabilization at any hospital participating in Medicare or Medicaid under EMTALA, regardless of immigration status or ability to pay. Emergency Medicaid covers only the acute stabilization episode, not ongoing care, prescriptions, follow-up appointments, or preventive services. For ongoing primary care, DACA recipients without comprehensive coverage should use Federally Qualified Health Centers (FQHCs) on a sliding-scale basis.

es.question: ?Pueden los beneficiarios de DACA comprar seguro de salud a traves del Mercado del ACA en 2026?
es.answer: No. La Regla Final de Integridad del Mercado CMS 2025, efectiva el 25 de agosto de 2025, elimino a los beneficiarios de DACA de la definicion de presencia legal para el Mercado del ACA. Los Dreamers no pueden inscribirse en Planes Calificados del Mercado, recibir Creditos Fiscales de Prima, reducciones de costos compartidos o acceder a Programas Basicos de Salud a traves del Mercado en 2026.

es.question: ?Cual es la mejor opcion de seguro de salud para los beneficiarios de DACA en 2026?
es.answer: Para la mayoria de los Dreamers, el seguro de salud del empleador a traves de un Documento de Autorizacion de Empleo (EAD) valido es la mejor opcion en 2026: cubre los 10 beneficios esenciales, los costos se comparten con el empleador y las primas se pagan antes de impuestos. Para los beneficiarios de DACA elegibles por ingresos en California, Nuevo Mexico, Washington u Oregon, los programas Medicaid estatales ofrecen cobertura integral a bajo costo o sin costo.

es.question: ?Los beneficiarios de DACA califican para el Credito Fiscal de Prima?
es.answer: No. Los beneficiarios de DACA no son elegibles para el Credito Fiscal de Prima (PTC) federal en 2026. La elegibilidad para el PTC requiere inscripcion en un plan del Mercado del ACA, y los beneficiarios de DACA no pueden inscribirse en planes del Mercado. Para los beneficiarios de DACA que recibieron APTC durante la ventana de noviembre de 2024 a agosto de 2025, se necesitara un Formulario 1095-A y una reconciliacion del Formulario 8962 en su declaracion de impuestos federales de 2025.

es.question: ?Pueden los beneficiarios de DACA usar una Cuenta de Ahorros para la Salud (HSA)?
es.answer: Si, si estan inscritos en un HDHP elegible para HSA. El estatus migratorio no afecta la elegibilidad para el HSA. Un HDHP en 2026 tiene un deducible minimo de $1,700 individual o $3,400 familiar (IRS Rev. Proc. 2025-19), y el limite de contribucion HSA es $4,400 individual o $8,750 familiar, mas $1,000 adicional si tiene 55 anos o mas. Las contribuciones HSA son deducibles de impuestos, crecen libres de impuestos y se pueden retirar libres de impuestos para gastos medicos calificados.

es.question: ?Sigue California cubriendo a los beneficiarios de DACA en Medi-Cal?
es.answer: Medi-Cal de California continua cubriendo a los beneficiarios de DACA que ya estaban inscritos antes del 1 de enero de 2026. Despues del 1 de enero de 2026, California congeló nuevas inscripciones en Medi-Cal para adultos indocumentados de 19 anos o mas. Los ninos menores de 19 anos y los individuos embarazados siguen siendo elegibles para solicitar Medi-Cal de cobertura completa independientemente del estatus migratorio. El limite de ingresos de Medi-Cal es el 138% del Nivel Federal de Pobreza de 2026: $22,025 para un individuo, $45,540 para una familia de cuatro.

es.question: ?Cuando pueden inscribirse los beneficiarios de DACA fuera de la inscripcion abierta?
es.answer: Para planes del empleador, los beneficiarios de DACA pueden inscribirse dentro de 30 a 60 dias de un evento calificador: obtener nuevo trabajo, perder cobertura, casarse, tener un hijo, o mudarse a un nuevo estado. Para programas Medicaid estatales en Nuevo Mexico, Washington y Oregon, la inscripcion es durante todo el ano sin restriccion de inscripcion abierta. Los FQHC no requieren inscripcion previa.

es.question: ?Pueden los beneficiarios de DACA reclamar una deduccion de seguro medico por trabajo por cuenta propia?
es.answer: Los beneficiarios de DACA que son propietarios unicos o contratistas 1099 con ingresos netos del trabajo por cuenta propia pueden reclamar la deduccion del Formulario 7206. En 2026, la cobertura calificada incluye planes del empleador, seguro privado fuera del Mercado o seguro estatal. Crucialmente, la deduccion del Formulario 7206 reduce el impuesto sobre la renta solamente y NO reduce el impuesto al trabajo por cuenta propia en el Schedule SE. La mayoria de los beneficiarios de DACA son empleados W-2; el Formulario 7206 no es relevante para ellos.

es.question: ?Que cobertura proporciona el Medicaid de emergencia para los beneficiarios de DACA?
es.answer: El Medicaid de emergencia proporciona reembolso federal a los hospitales por servicios de estabilizacion de emergencia proporcionados a personas que de otro modo calificarian para Medicaid pero por su estatus migratorio. Los beneficiarios de DACA pueden recibir estabilizacion de emergencia en cualquier hospital que participe en Medicare o Medicaid bajo EMTALA, independientemente del estatus migratorio. El Medicaid de emergencia cubre solo el episodio de estabilizacion aguda, no la atencion continua, recetas, citas de seguimiento ni servicios preventivos.
